doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Woody Herman and the war years
title: How he joined Woody Herman
summary: Woody phoned him; he signed a contract and flew to join the band, where he already knew Flip Phillips and Davy Tough joined at the same time.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: I love it. Tell me about how Woody Herman came about.

Well Woody was, I think that’s in my book, I mean really how I got in with Woody you mean? Well I think Flip must have recommended me. Because he’s the only one that I knew when I joined them. But Woody rang up. And he says, “This is Woody.” I says, “Woody who?” I loved it. You know I wasn’t, I don’t know. So he says, “We’re over in The Meadowbrook,” and he says, “we’re leaving tomorrow.” He says, “Why don’t you come over and sit in with us one set?” So I says, “Gee I can’t do that tonight, Woody.” He says, “Why?” I says, “Because it’s my kid’s birthday and I promised her I was going to be there.” He says it’s your kids, he repeated what I said. He says, “Okay I’ll tell you what you do. You go down to the Goldfarb,” and he gave me Radio City, blah, blah, blah, and he says, “And you go down there tomorrow and sign the contract and meet us in—” Now Flip says it was Cincinnati. I thought it was Detroit. And I forget what the name of the place was. But Flip says — well either case, that’s what I did, I went down there and then I took a plane, they gave me money for a plane, I flew in and sat down to play. The interesting — well but the only one I knew, Davy Tough, joined the band with me at the same time, and Flip, and I don’t know who else, but I got to know them. Oh I knew Flip, cause me and Flip used to do a lot of things together, little things.
I think Flip said he played with the Cliquot Eskimo — what is that?
The Cliquot Club Eskimos. Yes, you know it’s a ginger ale, Cliquot Club. That was the advertiser. Harry Reser. Are you sure he said that?
I think he did. Or maybe it was Jerry Jerome actually, I can’t really remember.
Flip played with Morgan. There was a Morgan he played with, and he played with Frankie Newton. That was his big thing. He was in in at Kelly’s Stable, but he played clarinet at that time.
